newsitem.title: USA: Fewer layoffs, record mergers in US '96--Challenger.
newsitem.headline: Fewer layoffs, record mergers in US '96--Challenger.

text.p: Despite a record volume of merger transactions, newly merged companies cut 46 percent fewer employees from their combined workforces in 1996 than in 1995, said Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc in a report on Monday.
Challenger said mergers accounted for 42,603 job cuts of the 1996 job-cut total of 477,147, against 72,083 of the 1995 job-cut total of 439,882.

"While corporate cost cutting is the genesis of many mergers, combined companies are re-examining their former stance about the disposability of people, and in many cases are choosing to find positions for as many experienced employees as possible," said John Challenger, executive vice president of Challenger, Gray & Christmas, an international outlplacement firm that tracks job-cut announcemnents daily.
Merger-related activity last year was "heavier" than most economists had expected, the report said,.
Securities Data Corp reported $658.8 billion worth of merger transactions were announced in 1996, it said.
"In the past, such heavy merger activity would have signaled massive job cuts," Challenger said.

"Today we are seeing a much different picture. Companies are recognizing that wholesale job slashing can ultimately hurt the bottom line by destroying corporate memory and lowering the morale of the remaining workforce," he said.
Challenger said merged entities should try to maintain a high standard of customer service and build their reputation as a way to hone their competitive edge.
"That can only be achieved when the workforce possesses a depth of experience and a commitment to the newly merged firm," Challenger added.
